subject: Mental Models
title: Antifragility
description: A quick, practical guide to Antifragility.

hook.text: A porcelain cup breaks when dropped. A muscle grows stronger when stressed. One is fragile.

buildup.text: Antifragility is the property of systems that improve when exposed to shocks, volatility, and stressors up to a point.

discovery.text: Taleb argued the opposite of fragile is not robust. Robust merely resists damage.

twist.text: Overprotecting a system makes it fragile.

climax.text: Expose yourself to small stressors regularly. Controlled volatility builds strength.

punchline.text: Small stresses build strength. Total comfort breeds weakness.

quiz.question: How does antifragile differ from robust?
options: Robust gains from stress while antifragile resists it
Antifragile improves from stress while robust merely resists it
